sections.why: Flooded Australian street under the ABC line that 10% of homes could be uninsurable by 2035 — climate putting housing beyond ordinary claims.
Aerial suburb pinned with per-home Bushfire, Flood and Cyclone risk gauges — each house scored for extreme weather.
Phone, laptop and tablet running Haven: 3D house, WebGL maps of Australia, and Read your report, with no player chrome.
CNBC: Anthropic CCO made a conscious decision not to put ads in Claude — values made visible when ads are absent.
One of the four spots: a coach mid-workout, the kind of fragile moment an ad should not interrupt.
Super Bowl LVI field — the actual Super Bowl buy for the black-comedy spots.
Rural Irish street with ‘9 out of 10 closed pubs are in rural Ireland’ and ‘the pub is the last center of the community.’
Empty pub, stacked chairs, and ‘SO WHAT IF A VILLAGE OWNED IT?’ — villagers saving the last pub.
Live Kilteely interview inside the real pub: ‘LOCAL LIMERICK COMMUNITY SAVES LAST PUB.’
News wall plus official statement: 12 tonnes of KitKat stolen in transit — the crisis.
Stolen KitKat Tracker grid: the public as detectives checking 8-digit batch codes.
Hands on a phone entering a KitKat batch number into the tracker UI.
Severance hallway — the entertainment brand being refreshed, not a generic logo hold.
Black-and-white App UI pill with the glass tv mark — the system at the moment you open the App.
Studio BTS of the physical glass  / + / tv sculptures on stands — in-camera, no CG mock.
Endless WAIT HERE / TRUSTED INSTITUTION queue — the old system you take control back from.
Suited man sprinting out of a low-poly NPC city — leaving the old system in a new film language.
Boardroom of in-camera 2D / low-poly NPC costumes — the physical game-world craft.
Burger, fries and a red fry box — ketchup belongs with fries, before the logo gag.
Keystone outline over the fry box and LOOK FAMILIAR? — the box shape is the Heinz logo.
New York City street billboard of the fry-box ad — outdoor execution in situ.
Woman in a transit hub listening to her phone — voice notes instead of meeting in person.
Bored man enduring a very long WhatsApp-style waveform — the over-long voice note that should have been a drink.
Building-side OOH of a giant stacked voice-note plus QR and ‘Podia ser uma Heineken.’
Tipped glass and the word Home — domestic disruption without sensational violence.
‘three words’ highlighted on a policy, ‘to help women escape’ — home insurance plus the clause.
Transit billboard in French highlighting violences conjugales and emergency relocation — the clause explained in public.
Clips-and-wires face-lift — beauty-marketing hype and fake-science extremes made physical.
Dystopian classroom facing The Periodic Fable / A scientific table with zero science — language itself on trial.
Clinical white classroom grid of uniformed students at identical desks — the film’s art direction.
